data.cultural_impact: The Ashvins are considered the bringers of the monsoon rains, and their month (Ashvin or Ashvin Shukla) is the seventh month in the Hindu calendar, known for its abundance with sweet ripe fruits. Their names are associated with the draft horses coupled with rain clouds which bring rain and prosperity. In our vibrant culture, we see Ashwina depicted as the givers of good fortune, health, happiness, and rejuvenation. The name is a reminder of their abundant blessings and the role they play in granting people's wishes.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Ashwina holds deep significance in conveying the divine and powerful presence of the celestial beings. It is believed that invoking the blessings of the twin horse gods can lead to physical and mental healing, positive energy and good fortune. Their ancient mythological roots evoke a deep sense of connection to tradition, religion and the divine. Ultimately, holding the name Ashwina is a daily reminder of their healing abilities and their role as guardians of good health and well-being.

historical_references.reference: The Ashwin Kumaras are a pair of deities in Hindu mythology, identified as the gods of the north-east directions and the harbingers of the monsoon rains. Their names come from the Ashwin star, which is part of the constellation of the same name in the northern hemisphere. They are represented as horse-headed beings, riding on horses or swans. The Ashwin Kumaras are often depicted as the physicians of the gods and the bringers of Ashwamedha Yajna, a horse sacrifice dedicated to Indra, the god of rain and thunder.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, circa 1500 BCE to present day

historical_references.reference: The Ashwinis are a tribe mentioned in the ancient Indian texts, particularly in the Mahabharata and the Rigveda. They are described as living in the region of the Punjab, and are associated with the Ashvins, the gods of rain and the horses. The Ashwinis are said to have been allies of the Pandava brothers, and helped them during the great battle of Kurukshetra. The Ashwin Kumaras, the divine representation of the Ashwinis, were also believed to bestow blessings upon the warriors before the battle.
